key_insight: Cryogenic terahertz nanoscopy can isolate and map the bulk photovoltaic effect in bilayer graphene, revealing how quantum geometry shapes photovoltaic response.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a high-resolution diagnostic tool for optimizing quantum-material photovoltaics and separating useful photocurrent from parasitic thermal/interface effects.
method: Dual-gated AB bilayer graphene measured with polarization-sensitive terahertz microscopy
Deep-subwavelength cryogenic imaging near the band-gap/THz resonance
Analyze angular, carrier-density, and temperature dependence of photocurrent
evidence_signal: The abstract reports spatially resolved BPVE with twofold polarization symmetry and theory agreement, plus carrier-density and temperature trends that expose trigonal warping and electron-hole asymmetry.
watch_item: The technique is cryogenic and material-specific, so translation to room-temperature devices and scalable device stacks may be challenging.
paper_title: Terahertz nanoscopy of quantum-geometric photovoltaics in bilayer graphene
